name: Storefront — duplicate checkout
note: This focused suite owns the shared cart preparation needed by both duplicate-cart and duplicate-checkout checks, so either check can run independently.

features.name: One cart, two tabs, one checkout

criteria.desc: the same item added from two tabs at once becomes one line of two
criteria.withheld: runs clean (2/2) but no mutant has been attempted against it yet.
criteria.statedBy: raises its quantity rather than adding a second line

criteria.desc: checking the same cart out twice at once produces one order
criteria.note: replayConcurrently replays each actor's LAST POST, so a racing tab must not touch the cart after its checkout is captured — that would overwrite the captured request with an add-to-cart. A third session on the same account fills the cart instead, leaving tab1 and tab2 holding nothing but their checkouts. A checkout carries no JSON body, so it never lands in lastWrites — the replay must select it by URL with the match option, or it silently races the last add-to-cart instead.
criteria.provenBy: checkout-not-idempotent (postgres-ecom-l1.json): stripping FOR UPDATE from the cart read at checkout made two replayed checkout requests each create an order — the criterion failed on its own assertion (expected exactly 1 order containing Keyboard, found 2). The unmutated app passes, refusing the second checkout with a 400.
criteria.withheld: uses the spec's named `checkout` action so it can be issued on either stack. It previously replayed a captured HTTP write, which SpacetimeDB never produces — that client writes over WebSocket — so the criterion reported INCONCLUSIVE there and the two backends were scored out of different totals. Points retained: it has already failed a mutant on the stacks that could run it.
criteria.statedBy: checking out twice must not produce two orders

features.note: Both tabs reach the item by search rather than trusting the storefront: earlier features in this suite buy things, which re-ranks the top ten. Each tab opens its OWN cart — panel state belongs to a browser context, not to the feature.
